rites.text: A mindful shielding technique that lets a creature strike with a thrust of sealed ward energy. It is the trademark practice of two antlered beasts who wield it in battle.

rites.name: Corirnes Seolliarnor
rites.text: A chilling trait that only creatures of one elemental nature may carry, granting them the power to lower the warmth of their surroundings. Few beings in the world possess it, and one of them can wield it in an enhanced form.

rites.name: Rornium Lianes
rites.text: A craft that lets one particular kind of bearer shift its form to match a chosen aspect of its nature. It is closely related to an older, broader form of the same art.

rites.name: Teostium
rites.text: A reflex-like technique that lets a certain kind of creature act before its rivals when it moves. Only one particular breed of slow, lumbering beast is able to use it.

rites.name: Leosarnum
rites.text: A bright refracted beam that a shining creature unleashes as one of its two signature techniques. It splits light into a dazzling spectrum that strikes its target.

rites.name: Vasus Mellaurus
rites.text: A mind-based strike that is a more forceful version of an earlier mental blow. It is the trademark technique of a cloned, legendary psychic creature.

rites.name: Orelanum Amestollium
rites.text: A mental gift that only a certain kind of creature can awaken, it appeared in a later age of the world. Two beings carry this gift, and one of them held it alone for a time.

rites.name: Vaulanum Millestanum
rites.text: A keeper of tamed beasts drills their creatures through repeated exercises to sharpen them for combat and to build the seasoning they need for public showings of skill.

rites.name: Sirnarus
rites.text: A reflective defensive quality that belongs only to a single radiant being and its two transformed guises. It works exactly like two other protective talents known in this world.

rites.name: Nellausor
rites.text: A mind-cutting technique wielded by one mechanical beast, a leaf-bladed machine. It is the signature strike of that creature, a sharp force that drives into the foe's thoughts.

rites.name: Celor
rites.text: A tuned strike of mind-force that breaks through the spirit and damages foes from afar. It is sold as a teachable disc that a creature can learn.

rites.name: Sinternium
rites.text: A tactic of rough, forceful contact used by creatures of a gentle, charming kind. It can be taught to others through a numbered training disc.

rites.name: Telosintor
rites.text: A rare hidden knack held only by two sludge-born creatures, allowing them to copy the gift of a close companion. It works exactly like a mirrored talent that catches what a partner loses.

rites.name: Seronanum Vintia
rites.text: A stored reserve of raw energy that only one kind of lumbering rock creature can channel. It is a special ability unique to that creature.

rites.name: Teosor
rites.text: A coordinated strike that a metal-bodied guardian and its engineer unleash together. It fires a bright burst of energy after the foe has been studied.

rites.name: Amentanum
rites.text: A modern trait that only the fairy-kin of this world can carry. It appears in the sixth age and is shared by a small handful of beings, two of which can transform into greater forms.

rites.name: Maullum
rites.text: A concealed inner talent that lets a bearer shift its own nature to match whatever it faces. Eight kinds of creature carry it, and one of them can awaken a greater form.

rites.name: Naulenum
rites.text: A charged gauntlet technique used by a single legendary guardian. Its strikes carry crackling energy that the user channels through the hands.

rites.name: Ameosia
rites.text: A companion-driven boost used during a containment effort, where a chosen creature lends its strength to fill a charging device. Each ally offers a different kind of aid, and the helper must rest briefly before it can be called again.

rites.name: Caunisium
rites.text: A swift leaping assault that a creature can learn from a recorded disc. The disc is numbered 21 in the modern training catalog of two regional tournaments.

rites.name: Amosum
rites.text: A common mental power that thinkers wield through inner force rather than muscle. Those who carry it tend to be sharp-minded and strong in mental strength but weaker in raw physical force.

rites.name: Leranum
rites.text: A cleansing technique that a strange sea-dwelling being is known to perform. It belongs to a restorative school of practice.

rites.name: Callanum
rites.text: A sharp, fast technique that strikes foes with a keen blade-like effect. It can be taught to certain creatures through a training disc.

rites.name: Laulum
rites.text: A powerful technique unlocked by a single creature, a signature art that only that one being can perform. It was revealed in a later era of the land's training practices.

rites.name: Vornines
rites.text: A withdrawal craft lets a fighter pull a companion back from the field and send a fresh one forward. It is a mechanic of ordered, deliberate exchange.

rites.name: Carnia Corosanum
rites.text: A heavy, tireless strike unleashed in tandem by a commander and his bound beast. It is the bond-technique belonging to one particular pairing of leader and lazy giant.

rites.name: Sianalus
rites.text: A knack held only by one heavy burrowing beast, it works like a bare-knuckle punch that slips past guards. It matches the effect of another similar technique.

rites.name: Lirus
rites.text: A raw, rebellious ability that belongs only to one kind of creature. Its power is named after a loud, defiant style of noise-driven music.

rites.name: Amiastor Vorialanum
rites.text: A companion-swapping technique that lets a wielder switch between several bonded creatures mid-battle. It is performed by pressing the down command, and it is shared across a leader and their partner beasts.

rites.name: Nosallium
rites.text: A soundless technique that quietly suspends a rival's next action, causing it to be delayed until after others have moved. A gentler counterpart allows the chosen target to act ahead of its turn.

rites.name: Valaurnanor
rites.text: A starry strike of cosmic force that a celestial rider unleashes in battle. It belongs to one ancient sky-bound warden and reflects the power of the heavens.

rites.name: Mistia
rites.text: A shielding craft practiced only by one mighty bonded guardian, drawn from an inner glow of spirit. It belongs to a late era of the world's history.

rites.name: Amoniror
rites.text: A distant tear that opens a shortcut through folded space. It is the defining technique of a shadowy trickster-spirit who wields it.

rites.name: Collus
rites.text: A shadowy power that belongs to one dread being and strengthens the dark-natured forces it commands. It is passed down through its bearer's presence alone.

rites.name: Meollus
rites.text: A cosmic-scale radiant technique drawn from the far-future heavens, unleashed by a star-born entity. It channels overwhelming light that scorches the sky itself.

rites.name: Amantaunia
rites.text: A far-future power granted only to certain tomorrow-born creatures, serving as the advanced counterpart to an older, ancient-style force.

rites.name: Nelliria
rites.text: A radiant technique that unleashes a column of pure light, channeled by a cosmic entity as one of its defining powers. It is a focused blast of luminous energy with a distinctive, dazzling form.

rites.name: Corases Valornum
rites.text: A cosmic dragon-kind technique that lets a great timeless creature unleash a thunderous roar. It belongs to one ancient guardian of the sky's hours.

rites.name: Raulia
rites.text: A gift held only by one singular guardian entity, it lets that being channel its inner might. It is an ability reserved solely for that single creature.

rites.name: Nesium
rites.text: Nesium is a concept within Breraston's Martial Realm, born in the Seventh Era of the Record, when the Three Futures fracture the ending into branches. It is shelved in the Library as one of the outcomes that every branch must answer for.

rites.name: Kalunaari
rites.text: Kalunaari is the concept of a branching future in Breraston, the moment when the ending splits and the Library shelves each outcome as its own volume. Its presence is felt during the Age of the first sovereign, when groves are still growing into kingdoms and every decision seems to open a new road. The concept is said to tilt the balance between the paths the living choose.
